entry_conditions: Peg is visibly retained, gripper remains closed, observed hole and TCP poses are finite, and a modest local correction appears reachable and collision-free. Entry may occur anywhere in the shared 1380-1500 alignment, descent, and engagement interval.
exit_conditions: Use only the unchanged task success geometry and a stable held pose. A small predicted residual or converged IK is not a new success criterion.
overlap_role: All assigned actions remain supervised, including 1,440 actions across the twelve [1380,1500) overlaps. Each target is encoded relative to its own action observation, supporting early and late predecessor switches.
successor_readiness: There is no learned successor. Continue closed-gripper stabilization after geometric success; if local commands drift from the destination, prefer the hole-frame policy rather than release.
failure_signatures: Repeated large local residuals; accumulating destination-relative drift; descent with lateral error; peg/TCP separation; IK nonconvergence or limits; collision; or stalled insertion. Re-anchoring is not demonstrated jam recovery.
continuation_guidance: Compose every executed slot with the fresh measured TCP and solve from fresh qpos. Do not accumulate residuals across denoising calls or from stale chunk context. Monitor observed hole-relative peg geometry externally.
limitations: The expected robustness to local perturbation is structural, not observed recovery evidence. Large fixture displacement, severe grasp errors, contacts, and jams are unsupported.
